Camila —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Attached are our consolidated redlines to Redwood's MSA (v3) and the draft order form. Our legal and ops teams flagged three high-priority items in the SLA/support section that we need to resolve before procurement can approve:

1) Uptime target: we marked 99.95% as the desired contractual uptime for the production environment. We saw Redwood's standard is 99.9% — can you confirm whether there is room to move to 99.95 for enterprise customers, or if there is an alternate higher-tier offering?

2) Maintenance blackout and patching windows: we need stricter guarantees around scheduled maintenance (max 4x per year, each window <= 2 hours) and a defined notification cadence (>=72 hours for planned maintenance). Our SREs also asked for a process for emergency patches that could be performed with 24-hour notice under tight security circumstances.

3) Service credits: the proposed credit formula in Section 5 is unclear when maintenance or force majeure applies. Please provide a clear credit matrix tying % downtime to credit % (we included a sample in OrderForm_Draft.xlsx). Also we expect a cap on credits per year and a one-click self-attestation path for incidents.

We're attaching a marked-up PDF and the order form with the credit matrix suggestion. If you could route this to your legal and platform ops folks and get back with recommended language (or proposed tradeoffs) by next Wednesday (11/08), that would keep our procurement timeline on track.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,

Camila / Team —

Thanks for pulling this together. I've reviewed Zephyr's redlines and drafted specific MSA language; attached is a marked-up MSA and a proposed SLA exhibit. Highlights of the recommended changes:

1) Definition of "Downtime":
- Proposed: "Downtime" means the aggregate duration within a monthly billing period during which the Redwood-hosted Service is unavailable to Customer for reasons other than Excluded Events (including, but not limited to: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer misconfiguration, customer's third-party network).
- Rationale: keep maintenance and other exclusions explicit so we don't pay credits for agreed/announced maintenance.

2) Uptime guarantee and scope:
- For Dedicated/Reserved Tiers: commit to 99.95% monthly uptime for the production model endpoint(s) specified in the Order Form, subject to documented maintenance windows and capacity constraints.
- For Hosted/Multi-tenant Tiers: commit to 99.9% monthly uptime.

3) Maintenance windows / notification:
- Planned maintenance: >=72 hours notice via email and the Console, with a maximum of 6 scheduled maintenance events per year for production (we can negotiate to fewer if required per account). Each event will be announced with expected duration; for liability we accept a single event duration up to 4 hours (not 2), and will work to batch disruptive work.
- Emergency security patches: Redwood may apply urgent changes with 24-hour notice when the change addresses verified CVEs or immediate operational risk; emergency patching is excluded from credits but will be followed by a full RCA and remediation timeline.

4) Credit matrix and caps:
- Attached SLA exhibit ties percentage monthly uptime ranges to credit % of monthly fees. Suggested cap: credits for a single month not to exceed 50% of that month's fees; aggregate credits in a 12-month period capped at 100% of 12 months' fees.

5) Response times / Severity ladder:
- P1 (Service Down): initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes during business hours; remediation target differs by tier and will be included in the exhibit; P2/P3 targets also proposed.

6) Self-attestation and evidence:
- We propose a clear incident evidence rubric and a process for customers to request credit with supporting logs. We can add a one-click claim in the Console but need to validate infeasible fraud risk.

Please see attached PDF with redlined MSA text and an SLA exhibit (Redwood_SLA_Credit_Matrix_v1.xlsx). I recommend we present the above to Zephyr with the following concessions: 99.95% for Dedicated only, 4-hour single-event cap, 6 planned events/year, and the credit caps listed.

If everyone agrees with that posture, I'll produce a tracked-change MSA to send back to Zephyr and propose a 30-minute call Thurs (11/04) to walk through the exhibit.

Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference
